newsitem.title: UK: UK output prices down 0.2% in June.
newsitem.headline: UK output prices down 0.2% in June.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) released the following provisional data on UK input and output prices in June. (Prev data in brackets)

Consensus of economists forecasts was for input prices to fall a seasonally adjusted 0.5 percent in June, leaving them 7.8 percent lower year-on-year. Unadjusted output prices were forecast flat and 1.1 percent higher year-on-year.
* The 0.2 percent monthly fall in unadjusted output prices and unadjusted core output prices was the largest since July 1996, when they also fell by 0.2 percent.

** The 1.1 percent rise in core output prices over the latest three months compared with the same period a year ago, was the highest since May 1996, when they also rose by 1.1. They have not risen by more than that since March last year.
The ONS said the 1.4 percent fall in unadjusted input prices reflected falls in the prices of crude oil and food manufacturing inputs.
Output prices excluding excise duties fell by an unadjusted 0.2 percent in June after a 0.2 percent increase in May. That leaves them 0.4 percent higher year-on-year versus 0.3 in May.

On a seasonally adjusted basis, output prices excluding excise duties edged up by 0.1 percent in June (+0.2 in May) and were 0.5 percent higher than a year earlier compared with a 0.3 percent year-on-year rise in May.
The ONS said if the budget increases in petrol duties were passed on in full it would add 0.5 percentage points to the all-manufacturing output producer price index.

The ONS said the publishing and printing industry had to cut prices to remain competitive in Europe because of European currency movements. Publishing and printing prices fell by 1.3 percent in the year to June.
